sections.overview: Sympistis funebris is a noctuid moth of boreal and alpine regions.
sections.identification: It is a small, dark moth; its forewing is about 11–12 mm long.
sections.habitat: It occurs in high-elevation alpine meadows and heathlands of western North America, and has a broader Holarctic range.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on shrubs and trees including bilberries (Vaccinium), birches (Betula) and crowberries (Empetrum).
sections.behavior: Adults fly by day and visit flowers; in the Pacific Northwest they are recorded mainly in July and August.
sections.reproduction: The regional account documents larval host plants but gives no further detail on egg-laying or development.
sections.ecology: Its larval hosts and flower-visiting adults connect it to alpine heath and meadow vegetation.
sections.conservation: The French observatory reports Least Concern in Europe; this regional status is not a global assessment.
